investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-29T09:10–09:17Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner never reached the agent-creation API call, so zero evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and every contract assertion failed.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM workload. The eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~140–143 seconds before the probe timed out, preventing createAgent() from being called and leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agent scheduling tier; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because evidence is empty
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, the effective capacity ceiling would drop. No source change evidence directly proves this, but the scheduler message confirms it.

TERTIARY — Insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster: the cluster may have been provisioned with only 2 peer-pod-capable nodes and the per-node VM limit is too low for concurrent eval runs. This is consistent with all three sibling checks failing simultaneously with the same message.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Eval runner scheduling multiple remote-agent pods concurrently without back-off: if remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all attempt to schedule pods at overlapping times, they could collectively exhaust the 2-node VM pool. The overlapping endedAt timestamps (09:12, 09:15, 09:17) are consistent with concurrent scheduling attempts.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output and violating the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that expose it. With 0/6 nodes available (2 due to insufficient VM capacity, 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch), the eval runner's createAgent call for a "remote" agent type cannot place a pod. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full ~143 s timeout, the probe exits without writing any evidence, and the contract validation fails on all four required evidence keys. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving none available for the eval probe pod. This is the most directly supported cause given the explicit scheduler message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node selector or affinity rule that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at VM capacity. If the affinity rules changed or nodes were re-labeled, the effective schedulable pool shrank.

Cluster under-provisioning for the kata peer-pods resource: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster is insufficient to absorb simultaneous eval probe pods plus any production workload, causing contention.

Eval probe scheduling conflict: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran in close succession and may have competed for the same limited VM slots, with remote-agent-create consuming the last available slot before remote-agent-state could schedule.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted at the time of the eval run would disprove the capacity-exhaustion hypothesis.

A successful remote-agent-state eval run (with all four evidence fields present) immediately after the failure window, without any cluster changes, would suggest a transient scheduling race rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod spec's node affinity/selector rules were recently changed to exclude more nodes, with no corresponding VM capacity increase, would shift the primary cause from exhaustion to misconfiguration.

Logs or events showing the createAgent API call failed before pod submission (e.g., an API authentication or quota error) would indicate the failure is upstream of the Kubernetes scheduler, not a VM capacity issue.
A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-runtime while remote-agent-state fails would suggest the issue is isolated to the state-polling probe rather than shared infrastructure capacity.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval check that queries kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, and fails fast with a descriptive capacity-exhaustion message rather than waiting for the scheduler timeout.

Add a dedicated eval for cluster node affinity/selector health that verifies the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's scheduling requirements, alerting when the eligible pool drops below a minimum threshold.
Add a kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization eval that tracks current VM slot usage vs. capacity and warns before exhaustion, enabling proactive remediation before eval probes begin failing.

Add a sibling-isolation eval variant that runs remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime sequentially (not concurrently) to detect whether simultaneous scheduling contention is a contributing factor.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment at 2026-06-29T09:10–09:17Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never became schedulable, the runner never reached the agent-creation API call, so zero evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and every contract assertion failed.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource capacity on the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable node exists for the peer-pod VM workload. The eval pod remained Unschedulable for ~140–143 seconds before the probe timed out, preventing createAgent() from being called and leaving all required evidence fields empty. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agent scheduling tier; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf ['running','idle','ready']; neither assertion could be evaluated because evidence is empty
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If this selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, the effective capacity ceiling would drop. No source change evidence directly proves this, but the scheduler message confirms it.

TERTIARY — Insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the cluster: the cluster may have been provisioned with only 2 peer-pod-capable nodes and the per-node VM limit is too low for concurrent eval runs. This is consistent with all three sibling checks failing simultaneously with the same message.

LOWER CONFIDENCE — Eval runner scheduling multiple remote-agent pods concurrently without back-off: if remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime all attempt to schedule pods at overlapping times, they could collectively exhaust the 2-node VM pool. The overlapping endedAt timestamps (09:12, 09:15, 09:17) are consistent with concurrent scheduling attempts.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Kata Peer-Pods VM Capacity Exhausted — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Unschedulable
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted by the eval runner was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 nodes that carry that resource, and node affinity/selector mismatches on the remaining 4 nodes. Because no pod could be scheduled, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, and the check produced zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the output and violating the expected-output contract defined in check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that expose it. With 0/6 nodes available (2 due to insufficient VM capacity, 4 due to node affinity/selector mismatch), the eval runner's createAgent call for a "remote" agent type cannot place a pod. The pod remains Unschedulable for the full ~143 s timeout, the probe exits without writing any evidence, and the contract validation fails on all four required evidence keys. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-traffic outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' and '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' across all 6 nodes, with no preemption victims available.

sibling.remote-agent-runtime: same scheduler rejection message as remote-agent-state, latencyMs=146453, confirming the condition persisted through the entire eval window ending at 2026-06-29T09:17:35.136Z.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}); no orgId, agentId, readyState, or state was written, consistent with the probe aborting before createAgent returned.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or a prior eval run left VM slots occupied, leaving none available for the eval probe pod. This is the most directly supported cause given the explicit scheduler message.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node selector or affinity rule that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 are already at VM capacity. If the affinity rules changed or nodes were re-labeled, the effective schedulable pool shrank.

Cluster under-provisioning for the kata peer-pods resource: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the cluster is insufficient to absorb simultaneous eval probe pods plus any production workload, causing contention.

Eval probe scheduling conflict: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran in close succession and may have competed for the same limited VM slots, with remote-agent-create consuming the last available slot before remote-agent-state could schedule.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Exhaustion: kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Depleted Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-29 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating zero schedulable nodes: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted during this eval window was stuck Unschedulable for ~140–143 seconds before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; this is localized to the observability eval environment targeting production-api.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 143s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=146453 endedAt=2026-06-29T09:17:35.136Z — eval ran for ~146s, consistent with the scheduler timeout window.
sibling.remote-agent-create: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=147537, endedAt=2026-06-29T09:12:38.151Z — earliest sibling failure confirms the scheduling problem predates the runtime check.

sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150532, endedAt=2026-06-29T09:15:08.682Z — all three checks share the same scheduler error, confirming a shared infrastructure dependency failure.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence keys were collected at all, consistent with the agent pod never reaching a running state.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing — confirms the probe never progressed past pod scheduling.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918, which must schedule a pod before any evidence can be gathered — scheduling failure blocks all downstream evidence collection.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:181-189: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false with outageLatencyMs=420000; the eval failed at ~146s, well within the latency budget, meaning the failure is a hard scheduling error, not a latency breach.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: the peer-pod VM quota is fully consumed, leaving no schedulable capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity. If the affinity rules were broadened or more matching nodes were added, scheduling might succeed.

TERTIARY — Concurrent or leaked remote agent pods consuming the kata.peerpods.io/vm quota: a prior eval run or user workload may have left pods running that hold the VM slots, preventing new scheduling. The scheduler message 'No preemption victims found' suggests no lower-priority pods exist to evict.

QUATERNARY — Cluster autoscaler not configured or not reacting in time for the eval window: if autoscaling for kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes is enabled but slow, the eval timeout (~146s) may expire before new node capacity is provisioned.

reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on all cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether the resource is still exhausted or has recovered since the eval run at 2026-06-29T09:15–09:17Z.

reproductionSteps.details: Identify whether leaked or long-running remote agent pods are holding the VM quota.

reproductionSteps.label: Check for pending remote agent pods stuck in Unschedulable state
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether additional pods from the eval or from user workloads are still queued.

reproductionSteps.label: Review node affinity rules applied to remote agent pods
reproductionSteps.details: Inspect the pod spec generated by createAgent in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to confirm which node selector or affinity labels are required, and verify how many nodes in the cluster carry those labels.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Kubernetes pod scheduling layer (kata.peerpods.io/vm resource)
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler explicitly reports Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity, blocking all remote agent pod creation (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents — Node affinity/selector configuration
affectedAreas.reason: 4 of 6 cluster nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, concentrating all scheduling pressure onto 2 nodes that are already at VM capacity (evidence: failed-check.message).

affectedAreas.label: Eval check: remote-agent-create (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: First sibling to fail at 09:12:38Z; the createAgent call for a remote agent type could not schedule a pod (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-create).

affectedAreas.label: Eval check: remote-agent-state (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Second sibling to fail at 09:15:08Z with the same Unschedulable message (evidence: sibling.remote-agent-state).

affectedAreas.label: Eval check: remote-agent-runtime (production-api)
affectedAreas.reason: Primary failing check; runner branch at line 1913–1918 calls createAgent for a remote agent, which never scheduled, leaving all 5 required evidence fields unmet (evidence: failed-check.message, failed-check.evidence, expected-output.missing-required-evidence, source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918).

affectedAreas.label: Expected-output contract: remote-agent-runtime
affectedAreas.reason: All 5 required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) and the message assertion ('hello from aura') are unmet because the pod never started (evidence: expected-output.contract, expected-output.missing-required-evidence, source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:262-270).

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource usage across all cluster nodes to determine whether the quota is still exhausted or has self-recovered since 2026-06-29T09:17Z.
Identify and terminate any leaked or zombie remote agent pods (from prior eval runs or user workloads) that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active use.

Review the node affinity/selector rules applied to remote agent pods: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible, creating a narrow scheduling target. Evaluate whether additional nodes should be labeled to match the affinity, or whether the VM quota on existing nodes should be increased.

Determine the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota per node and the maximum number of concurrent remote agent pods the cluster can support. If the eval harness creates multiple pods in parallel (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime ran within ~5 minutes of each other), the combined demand may exceed the quota.
Investigate whether a cluster autoscaler is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes and, if so, why it did not provision additional capacity within the ~146s eval window.

Once scheduling capacity is restored, re-run the full remote-agents eval suite to confirm all three checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) pass and produce the expected evidence fields.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval to confirm reproducibility
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Determines whether the scheduling failure is persistent or was transient at the time of the 2026-06-29T09:15Z run.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run all three remote-agents checks together to confirm shared dependency
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether all three checks continue to fail with the same Unschedulable message, validating the shared scheduling dependency hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels to verify affinity-matching node count
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms how many nodes carry the labels required by the remote agent pod's node affinity/selector, and whether the 2-node constraint is expected or a misconfiguration.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check for pending or stuck remote agent pods from prior eval runs
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether prior eval runs left pods in Pending state that are holding VM quota without releasing it.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes showed available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the affinity-matching nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion theory would be weakened and a different cause (e.g., API auth failure, network partition) would need to be investigated.

If the remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state checks had passed while remote-agent-runtime failed, a shared scheduling exhaustion cause would be disproved and the failure would be localized to the runtime check's specific pod spec or configuration.
If the eval runner logs showed the pod was scheduled but the agent process crashed or returned an unexpected response, the root cause would shift from scheduling to application runtime behavior.

If a passing run of any remote-agents check is found in the history (lastPassingAt is currently null with previousRunCount=0), it would indicate this is a first-run failure that may be environmental or configuration-related rather than a regression.

If the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota was intentionally reduced or the node affinity rules were recently tightened, and that change is reflected in cluster configuration history, it would provide an alternative infrastructure-change cause.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all cluster nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agents eval suite that verifies at least one node with the required affinity labels has available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting createAgent, and reports a distinct 'capacity-unavailable' status rather than a generic timeout failure.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that lists all remote agent pods older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found in Running or Pending state without an active eval session, to catch quota-holding zombie pods early.

Extend the remote-agent-create check to capture and surface the Kubernetes scheduler event message as structured evidence (e.g., schedulerMessage, unschedulableReason) so future failures are immediately diagnosable without manual kubectl inspection.
